title: Shoulder examination: impingement
stem: Cubicle 17. Miss Ali, 28, a netball player, has had right shoulder pain since a match yesterday, worse lifting her arm overhead. Examine her shoulder and explain your findings and management.
notes:
Checked against BESS/BOA guidance on subacromial shoulder pain (2021) and standard examination technique.

Look (front, side, back: asymmetry, wasting of supraspinatus/infraspinatus, winging, swelling), feel (SC joint, clavicle, AC joint, coracoid, acromion, greater tuberosity, bicipital groove, spine of scapula), move (active then passive: flexion, extension, abduction with painful arc 60–120° in subacromial pain; external rotation — loss of passive external rotation suggests frozen shoulder or OA; internal rotation), special tests: supraspinatus (empty can/Jobe), infraspinatus/teres minor (resisted external rotation), subscapularis (lift-off, belly press), impingement (Neer, Hawkins–Kennedy), biceps (Speed's), AC joint (scarf test), instability (apprehension/relocation, sulcus). Examine the neck and neurovascular status (axillary nerve).

Subacromial pain is managed with analgesia, activity modification and physiotherapy; injections for persisting symptoms; imaging if trauma, weakness (cuff tear) or no improvement. An acute traumatic cuff tear with weakness needs early (within weeks) orthopaedic referral. Your shoulder notes are thorough and match this.

steps.label: Examine the shoulder
steps.hint: Introduce and expose; look, feel, move, special tests, neck, neurovascular.

Start.t: Introduce, consent, offer analgesia, expose both shoulders
Start.r: Ready, sitting upright, both shoulders exposed.
Start.mark: Introduces, consents and exposes both shoulders

Look.t: Inspect front, side and back; wall push for winging
Look.mark: Inspects from all sides including winging

Feel.t: SC joint, clavicle, AC joint, acromion, greater tuberosity, bicipital groove
Feel.r: Tender just below the anterolateral acromion. AC joint not tender.

Move.r: Pain between 70° and 120° of abduction, eases above that.
Full and painless — not frozen shoulder.

Complete.t: Neck movements; sensation over the badge area; pulses
Complete.mark: Examines the neck and neurovascular status

steps.ask: Thank you. Please present your findings and your plan.
steps.label: Present and plan
steps.hint: Subacromial pain (impingement/cuff tendinopathy), cuff strength intact; conservative plan.

opts.t: Subacromial pain / rotator cuff tendinopathy: painful arc, positive Neer and Hawkins, strength intact
opts.mark: Gives the diagnosis supported by findings

opts.t: X-ray not needed without trauma or red flags; analgesia, relative rest from overhead activity, physiotherapy; review if not improving
Urgent MRI and orthopaedic surgery tonight
opts.r: Strength is intact; conservative management first.

qs.q: Loss of passive external rotation suggests…
wrong: Acromioclavicular joint sprain after a fall

qs.q: Painful arc of subacromial pain is…
Nerve at risk after shoulder dislocation and how to test it?
wrong: Radial — wrist drop and first web space
Ulnar — finger abduction and little finger
Median — thumb opposition and index pulp

badge.name: Rotator
badge.flavor: Painful arc, Neer and Hawkins, strength intact: physio first.

options: Passive forward flexion, arm internally rotated
Resisted external rotation with the elbow at the side
Lifting the hand off the lower back
Adducting the arm across the chest, elbow bent

cards.q: Acute traumatic cuff tear with weakness in a young patient needs…

cards.why: Resisted forward flexion with a supinated arm.
